Petitioner :- Rahul Rai
Respondent :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Revenue , Civil Secrt. U.P. Lucknow And Ot
Counsel for Petitioner :- Bhanu Pratap Singhbisen

Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.,Avnish Kumar Singh,Ratnesh Chandra
Hon'ble Mrs. Sangeeta Chandra,J.
Hon'ble Manish Kumar,J.
1. Heard.
2.

This petition has been filed with the following main relief:
"i. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of Mandamus commanding the opp.
parties concerned to provide the fair and proper compensation of the residential plot of the petitioner which is part of land khasra no.624 area 1000 sq.ft. i.e. 92.936 sq.
metres situated in village Kaliya Khera, Tehsil Sarojani Nagar, District Lucnkow, as well as also interest in accordance with law since the acquisition of the plot of the petitioner till the actual date of payment of compensation in the interest of justice, to the petitioner."
3. It is the case of the petitioner that the State Government had acquired land of Gata No.624 situated in Village Kaliya Khera, Tehsil Sarojani Nagar, District Lucknow, on the basis of a registered sale deed by the Lucknow Development Authority.

The petitioner has approached the Rahul Rai vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Revenue , ... on 16 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36644935/
1 respondents for fair compensation from time to time as his plot was residential in nature.

entities.text: Rahul Rai vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Revenue
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
However,
the respondents have not given fair compensation till date.
Although the money was transferred in his account as a result of such acquisition, he believes the said compensation to be too less

,
therefore, this writ petition has been filed.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner has referred to an application filed by the petitioner on 22.09.2022 and its annexure-2 which shows the estimate/ calculation made by the respondents themselves with regard to the land acquired by them.
The total amount as due has been mentioned as Rs.26,76,412/-, however only 4,19,000/- has been given to the petitioner.
Rs. 22,57,403/- is still remaining to be paid.

5. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the State Respondents, on the basis of written instructions sent by the Additional District Magistrate (Land Acquisition), Lucknow, says that the petitioner has been paid compensation through voucher dated 06.08.2022 and the money has been credited in his bank account.
Only 92 sq. mtrs. of petitioner's land was acquired.

As per the Award,
Rs.560/- was payable per sq. mtr.
As a consequence, the compensation of Rs.51,520/- was determined as fair value of the land which was multiplied by two and 100% solatium on the same was also determined.
As a result, total compensation payable to the petitioner was Rs.1,88,160/-, of which Rs.18,631/- was paid at the time of notification under Section 4/16.
After calculating interest on the remaining amount at the rate of 9% per annum, Rs.4,19,000/- alone is payable to the petitioner which was paid in his bank account.
6. This Court finds that the respondents after calculation of fair compensation under the Act of 2013 have paid the same in the Bank account of the petitioner on 08.08.2022.
If the petitioner is aggrieved by less compensation and he wishes for its enhancement, the appropriate remedy for the petitioner is to file a Reference under Section 64 before the Collector.
If such an application is made by the petitioner for Reference for enhancement, the Collector shall make Reference to the appropriate authority within 30 days of receipt of such application.
7. The writ petition stands disposed of.
